item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"medium","summary":"A is the less risky patch, though neither is merge-ready because both violate central frozen-contract requirements.","reasons":["A directly verifies that Upload retries streamed, non-seekable content and preserves multipart field name, filename, and content; B does not test Upload retry behavior itself.","B globally buffers every otherwise non-replayable Raw.Do body. Its makeBodyReplayable silently ignores io.ReadAll errors and can send a truncated body, while also replacing an io.ReadCloser without closing it.","A's unrelated Raw.Do change is narrower: it only adds replay support for io.ReadSeeker bodies and leaves non-seekable streams unchanged.","A reports empty-filename and nil-content validation separately, giving clearer error semantics than B's combined error."],"risks_a":["Upload has the wrong signature: it accepts UploadFileOption instead of the required FilesOption.","Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its request, response, option, and error handling.","It adds forbidden association options and extends multipartbody with NewForm instead of directly reusing NewFile as required by the contract scope limitation; it also changes unrelated retry machinery and documentation around Add/Raw.Do retries beyond scope accommodation cited in contract. It also lacks the required source-reader-error test."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong signature, accepting AddFileOption rather than FilesOption, and adds forbidden association and query APIs.","Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and calls Raw.Do directly, duplicating established behavior.","It does not directly reuse multipartbody.NewFile, adding NewFileWithFields instead, and lacks required Upload streamed-retry and source-reader-error tests. Its broad Raw.Do buffering refactor violates scope and can suppress reader failures, leak replaced bodies, and unexpectedly buffer arbitrary streams in memory."]}
